research.report:
# Julius Muth: Publicly Documented Professional Activities at revel8

## Scope and assessment

Julius Muth is publicly identified as a founder and business leader of revel8, a company developing security-awareness training around AI-enabled impersonation and social engineering. The most precise title in revel8’s company factsheet is **Co-CEO**, alongside fellow founder Tom Müller; revel8’s author page instead calls Muth **Co-Founder & CEO**. The sources establish his leadership and public-facing work more clearly than they establish a formal division of responsibilities between the two co-CEOs. ([revel8, 2026a](https://www.revel8.ai/grounding); [revel8, n.d.-a](https://www.revel8.ai/author-julius))

**Overall assessment:** Muth’s documented contribution is principally in company formation, commercial positioning, fundraising communications, and explaining revel8’s approach to potential customers and the cybersecurity community. His prior sales experience is supported by an investor interview and a podcast description. By contrast, the supplied material does **not** establish that he personally authored peer-reviewed research, engineered the platform, or delivered a particular conference presentation. Those distinctions matter when assessing his professional record. ([Locher, 2024](https://news.merantix-capital.com/p/saving-companies-from-cyber-scammers); [Marketing From Zero To One, n.d.](https://soundcloud.com/marketing_021/juliusmuth); [SANS Institute, n.d.](https://www.sans.org/profiles/julius-muth))

The evidence below is limited to the supplied public sources. Dates are publication or event dates **where the source provides them**; an undated page, an episode without a visible release date, or a relative social-media timestamp is not treated as proof of an exact date.

## Professional background and founding role

### Earlier work and the Company Shield origin

A September 3, 2024, Merantix Capital interview reports that Muth and Tom Müller met while working at Celonis: Muth in **sales** and Müller in **engineering**. According to that account, they discussed an AI-enabled approach to employee cybersecurity training while based in Celonis’s Madrid office. The venture initially operated as **Company Shield**, offering clients continuing training through automated, AI-generated simulations modeled on real scams. This is useful evidence for Muth’s sales background and for the venture’s early product concept, although Merantix was also an investor and its account should be read with that relationship in mind. ([Locher, 2024](https://news.merantix-capital.com/p/saving-companies-from-cyber-scammers))

The description of a *Marketing From Zero To One* podcast episode additionally names **PwC, Celonis, and Project A** among Muth’s earlier professional stations. Its chapter list points to discussion of international sales at Celonis, startup projects during his studies, structured testing of founding ideas, and an improvised first customer offering. These details are **reported in the episode description**, not independently verified employment dates, job titles, or transcripts of every statement made in the recording. The supplied SoundCloud page does not show a publication date, so the episode cannot responsibly be placed on a precise timeline. ([Marketing From Zero To One, n.d.](https://soundcloud.com/marketing_021/juliusmuth))

revel8’s factsheet names **Muth and Müller as Co-CEOs** and **Robert Seilbeck as CTO**. It gives the company’s former name as Company Shield and says it was founded in **2024**. That year is also consistent with the September 2025 Tech.eu account, but one September 2025 Vestbee article says the venture was “launched in 2023.” The supplied sources do not explain whether Vestbee meant early development rather than formal founding; **2024 is the better-supported formal founding year**, while the discrepancy remains unresolved. ([revel8, 2026a](https://www.revel8.ai/grounding); [Djurickovic, 2025](https://tech.eu/2025/09/25/revel8-nets-eur7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [Laoun, 2025](https://vestbee.com/insights/articles/revel8-secures-7-m))

### Business and go-to-market emphasis

Muth’s revel8 author biography presents him as focused on cybersecurity **go-to-market strategy**, enterprise positioning, B2B software sales, and product–market fit in response to AI-driven phishing, deepfakes, and social engineering. That is the company’s description of his expertise, rather than independent proof of any particular sales outcome. It nevertheless aligns with the independently reported fact that he previously worked in Celonis sales and with his prominent role in revel8’s funding and product announcements. ([revel8, n.d.-a](https://www.revel8.ai/author-julius); [Locher, 2024](https://news.merantix-capital.com/p/saving-companies-from-cyber-scammers); [Djurickovic, 2025](https://tech.eu/2025/09/25/revel8-nets-eur7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks))

The podcast description provides a more concrete account of early commercialization: its listed topics include testing ideas through mailed letters and personal pitches, securing a first paying customer with an improvised minimum viable product, and combining letters, email, and calls in business-to-business outreach. Because these are episode-summary claims, they document topics Muth publicly discussed, **not independently measured conversion rates or a validated sales methodology**. ([Marketing From Zero To One, n.d.](https://soundcloud.com/marketing_021/juliusmuth))

## Announced projects and product direction

### AI-driven employee training

The central publicly announced project is revel8’s security-awareness platform. The 2024 Merantix interview described Company Shield’s early model as **continuous, automated simulations of real-world scams**, offered as an alternative to one-off online training. By September 2025, revel8’s funding coverage described adaptive employee simulations across channels including **email, SMS, voice, and video**. These sources document the company’s stated product proposition and evolution in presentation; they do not, by themselves, demonstrate comparative effectiveness against conventional training. ([Locher, 2024](https://news.merantix-capital.com/p/saving-companies-from-cyber-scammers); [Laoun, 2025](https://vestbee.com/insights/articles/revel8-secures-7-m))

In coverage of the 2025 funding round, Muth argued that realistic replicas of current scams were preferable to traditional e-learning. revel8 also described its aim as training **10 million “human firewalls.”** The first point is his attributed assessment; the second is a **company ambition, not a reported number of people trained**. A separate interview-based funding article specifies an ambition to reach that number by **2028**, which likewise remains a target. ([revel8, 2025a](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [Tech Funding News, n.d.](https://techfundingnews.com/revel8-raises-7m-ai-powered-human-firewalls-cybersecurity))

The company’s August 2026 factsheet describes a broader platform direction: recommended countermeasures through a **Mitigation Center**, group-based reporting intended to accommodate works councils, partner-oriented multi-tenant administration, and audit-related reporting. It also lists hosting on Germany’s **STACKIT** cloud. These are **revel8’s published product and infrastructure assertions**, not independent audits of functionality, legal compliance, or security outcomes. The factsheet says the company reviewed **more than 100,000 simulations** in its 2025 threat work, including **more than 10,000 vishing simulations**; those are company-reported analysis counts rather than an independently verified customer or effectiveness measure. ([revel8, 2026a](https://www.revel8.ai/grounding))

### Locations and organizational development

Location descriptions change across the available accounts. revel8’s September 2025 announcement called the company **Berlin-headquartered** and said a move to Munich was planned for early 2026; its August 2026 factsheet identifies the company as based in **Munich**. This is best understood as a dated change in how the company described its location, not evidence that the earlier reporting was necessarily false. An undated SANS profile likewise describes revel8 as Munich-based and says it employed **35 people**, but supplies no as-of date for that headcount. ([revel8, 2025a](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [revel8, 2026a](https://www.revel8.ai/grounding); [SANS Institute, n.d.](https://www.sans.org/profiles/julius-muth))

| Publicly documented development | Date established by source | What the evidence supports |
|---|---|---|
| Company Shield’s continuous scam-simulation concept and Muth’s Celonis sales background | **September 3, 2024** | An investor-published interview describing the venture’s early proposition and founding context. ([Locher, 2024](https://news.merantix-capital.com/p/saving-companies-from-cyber-scammers)) |
| €5.7 million seed round, bringing disclosed total funding to €7 million | **September 25, 2025** | A company announcement corroborated by contemporaneous technology reporting. ([revel8, 2025a](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [Djurickovic, 2025](https://tech.eu/2025/09/25/revel8-nets-eur7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks)) |
| Published company factsheet identifying Muth and Müller as Co-CEOs and detailing the platform | **Created July 15, 2026; updated August 3, 2026** | Current company self-description as of the stated update, not third-party verification of every product claim. ([revel8, 2026a](https://www.revel8.ai/grounding)) |
| Team expansion in growth and product roles | **No exact publication date supplied** | Muth publicly welcomed new joiners and connected the hiring to the forthcoming roadmap; LinkedIn’s relative timestamp does not establish a reliable calendar date here. ([Muth, n.d.](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/julius-muth_so-excited-to-see-the-revel8-team-expanding-activity-7439948140998430721-yIL7)) |

## Presentations, interviews, and published writing

### Interviews and speaking evidence

The **September 3, 2024 Merantix interview** is the clearest dated interview in the supplied record. It addresses how Company Shield’s training works and the founders’ view of AI-enabled scams. Its value lies in documenting Muth’s public explanation of the venture at an early stage, while its investor-published setting should be considered when weighing promotional claims. ([Locher, 2024](https://news.merantix-capital.com/p/saving-companies-from-cyber-scammers))

The *Marketing From Zero To One* episode identifies Muth as a guest and supplies chapter markers for discussion of his career, founding experiments, AI-powered simulations, internal AI use, and a proposed **“AI twin”** product direction. The “AI twin” should be treated as a topic or prospective direction described by the podcast, **not proof that a finished feature was released**. No release date is visible in the provided page content. ([Marketing From Zero To One, n.d.](https://soundcloud.com/marketing_021/juliusmuth))

SANS Institute maintains a contributor profile for Muth but describes its “Speaker / Contributor” designation broadly: it can encompass events, presentations, written content, or other community resources. SANS explicitly says such people are **not SANS employees, instructors, or affiliates**. The supplied profile names **no specific conference, session, event date, talk title, or technical presentation**. Accordingly, his appearance on that page supports an external contributor association, **not a verified claim that he delivered a particular SANS conference talk**. ([SANS Institute, n.d.](https://www.sans.org/profiles/julius-muth))

### Articles and technical-work limits

revel8’s author page lists Muth under several dated pieces. The visible titles include **“Leading Security Beyond Compliance: Lessons from Dr. Daniel Schatz”** on **January 30, 2026**; **“Jaya Baloo on Cyber Priorities in an AI-Driven World”** on **November 25, 2025**; **“How Dr. Peter Dornheim is redefining cybersecurity culture”** on **November 6, 2025**; and **“Vishing 101: How to Protect from AI Voice Phishing”** on **October 31, 2025**. These entries establish what revel8’s site attributes to Muth and the dates displayed there. The supplied excerpts do not include the full articles, so their methods, findings, and whether the “CISO Portraits” involved direct interviews cannot be assessed from these titles alone. ([revel8, n.d.-a](https://www.revel8.ai/author-julius))

The same author page lists **“Cybersecurity Awareness Month 2025: Turning awareness into Action”** on **October 9, 2025**, as well as earlier CISO-focused pieces dated **July 29, June 23, and June 18, 2025**. It also attributes the **September 25, 2025 funding announcement** to him. Collectively, this is evidence of a sustained public communications role spanning security awareness, cybersecurity leadership, and company news; it is **not equivalent to evidence of personally authored software, patents, or peer-reviewed technical research**. ([revel8, n.d.-a](https://www.revel8.ai/author-julius))

**Technical-work finding:** The supplied sources document technical *subjects*—vishing, deepfakes, multimodal attack simulations, and adaptive training—and reveal company-level product claims. They do not identify a peer-reviewed paper, patent, code repository, technical standard, or independently evaluated study authored by Muth. His visible technical publication footprint in this record is therefore best characterized as **practitioner-oriented company writing and product explanation**, with the limits of the available article excerpts noted above. ([revel8, n.d.-a](https://www.revel8.ai/author-julius); [revel8, 2026a](https://www.revel8.ai/grounding); [SANS Institute, n.d.](https://www.sans.org/profiles/julius-muth))

## Funding and recent company announcements

On **September 25, 2025**, revel8 announced a **€5.7 million seed round**, bringing reported funding to **€7 million total**. Contemporaneous Tech.eu coverage identifies **Peak** as the lead investor, with **Fortino Capital, Merantix Capital, and angel investors** participating. This is the strongest dated financial milestone in the supplied record because the company’s announcement and independent contemporaneous reporting agree on the principal figures. Total funding and the new round should not be conflated: **€7 million is cumulative funding; €5.7 million is the seed round**. ([revel8, 2025a](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [Djurickovic, 2025](https://tech.eu/2025/09/25/revel8-nets-eur7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks))

The company said the capital would support **team expansion, stronger enterprise features, and international growth**. Muth framed the investment as resources for building defenses against emerging threats. Those statements document management’s intended use of funding; the supplied sources do not establish how much was ultimately spent in each area or whether the proposed international expansion was completed. ([revel8, 2025a](https://www.revel8.ai/blog/revel8-secures-eu7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks))

Muth later shared a LinkedIn post welcoming five recent colleagues whom the associated company post said would work on **growth and product**. He described their arrival as important to the upcoming roadmap. The supplied LinkedIn extract displays only a relative age for the post; without a dependable capture date, assigning it a precise publication month or year would overstate the evidence. The post supports a narrower conclusion: **Muth publicly participated in announcing team expansion**, not that particular unreleased projects had been completed. ([Muth, n.d.](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/julius-muth_so-excited-to-see-the-revel8-team-expanding-activity-7439948140998430721-yIL7))

## Evidence-based conclusion

The record supports a coherent professional profile: Muth brought a documented **Celonis sales background** to the formation of Company Shield/revel8; is identified by revel8 as a **Co-CEO**; has publicly explained its simulated-attack training model; appeared in an investor interview and a business podcast; contributed company-site articles; and served as a visible spokesperson around the **September 2025 €5.7 million seed round**. The available evidence supports calling him a **commercial and public-facing founder of an AI-security-awareness company**. It does **not** support stronger claims that he personally built its technical systems, proved its training efficacy through published research, or presented a specified conference session. That narrower characterization is both more informative and more defensible than treating company ambitions or promotional descriptions as accomplished individual achievements. ([Locher, 2024](https://news.merantix-capital.com/p/saving-companies-from-cyber-scammers); [revel8, 2026a](https://www.revel8.ai/grounding); [revel8, n.d.-a](https://www.revel8.ai/author-julius); [Djurickovic, 2025](https://tech.eu/2025/09/25/revel8-nets-eur7-million-to-fight-ai-powered-cyberattacks); [SANS Institute, n.d.](https://www.sans.org/profiles/julius-muth))
